title: Deep learning reveals prognostic information beyond AJCC stage in routine histopathology of early-stage melanoma: the population-based D-ESMEL study
zh_title: 深度学习从早期黑色素瘤常规病理揭示超出AJCC分期的预后信息
summary: 基于荷兰人群D-ESMEL研究的预印本，用全切片图像深度学习提取早期黑色素瘤预后信息，在5500例以上人群中验证。
key_points: 发现集328例，按已知预后因素匹配
验证队列基于5500例以上患者的巢式病例对照

reason: 人群基础大样本外部验证，但为预印本、回顾性病例对照设计
abstract: Of all melanoma patients who develop distant metastasis over time, 41% were initially diagnosed with stage I/II. More accurate prognostic models are needed to select patients for potential (neo)adjuvant therapy. We hypothesise that histopathological features in whole slide images (WSIs) from primary early-stage melanomas provide additional information beyond American Joint Committee on Cancer (AJCC) stage. We utilised data from the population-based Dutch Early-Stage Melanoma (D-ESMEL) study. This included a discovery set (n=328) of case-control sets matched on follow-up time and known prognostic features (i.e. Breslow thickness, ulceration, age, and sex) and a validation cohort based on >5,500 patients following a nested case-control (NCC) design with stage-matched controls (n=266). We developed an end-to-end deep learning workflow to automatically extract relevant patches from WSIs and predict patient-level metastatic risk based on histopathological features independent of AJCC stage. The discovery set served as a training set for the workflow using 10-fold cross-validation. The prognostic performance of this model and its independence from clinical risk factors was evaluated in the validation cohort using odds ratios (OR) and the weighted C-index. We achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.88 (mean: 0.81; 95% CI: 0.77-0.85) in the best validation fold of the discovery set. In the validation cohort, metastatic risk predictions from the deep learning model were an independent prognostic factor (adjusted OR: 1.97; p<0.01). Combining the deep learning predictions (C-index: 0.86) with AJCC stage (C-index: 0.80) yielded the highest C-index of 0.87, significantly improving the C-index compared to AJCC stage alone (p<0.001). Our histopathology-based deep learning model was rigorously evaluated in a population-based cohort and demonstrated added prognostic value beyond AJCC stage. Further investigations of the underlying biological features could improve clinical decision making and patient outcomes.
zh_abstract: 在所有随时间发生远处转移的黑色素瘤患者中，41% 初诊时为 I/II 期。需要更准确的预后模型来选择可能接受（新）辅助治疗的患者。我们假设，原发性早期黑色素瘤全切片图像（WSIs）中的组织病理学特征可提供超出美国癌症联合委员会（AJCC）分期的额外信息。我们使用了基于人群的荷兰早期黑色素瘤（D-ESMEL）研究的数据。该研究包括一个发现集（n=328），由按随访时间和已知预后特征（即 Breslow 厚度、溃疡、年龄和性别）匹配的病例-对照集组成；以及一个基于 >5,500 例患者的验证队列，采用巢式病例对照（NCC）设计并设置分期匹配的对照（n=266）。我们开发了一个端到端深度学习工作流程，从 WSIs 中自动提取相关图像块，并基于独立于 AJCC 分期的组织病理学特征预测患者水平的转移风险。发现集作为该工作流程的训练集，采用 10 折交叉验证。在验证队列中，使用比值比（OR）和加权 C 指数评估该模型的预后性能及其独立于临床风险因素的程度。在发现集的最佳验证折中，我们达到了 0.88 的平衡准确率（均值：0.81；95% CI：0.77-0.85）。在验证队列中，深度学习模型的转移风险预测是一个独立预后因素（校正 OR：1.97；p<0.01）。将深度学习预测（C 指数：0.86）与 AJCC 分期（C 指数：0.80）结合，得到最高的 C 指数 0.87，与单独 AJCC 分期相比显著提高了 C 指数（p<0.001）。我们基于组织病理学的深度学习模型在基于人群的队列中经过严格评估，并显示出超出 AJCC 分期的附加预后价值。对潜在生物学特征的进一步研究可改善临床决策和患者结局。

title: DINOv2 for PET: A Pre-Training Domain Benchmark Across Classification, Segmentation, and Prognosis
zh_title: PET-DINOv2-2D：PET影像自监督预训练领域基准
summary: arXiv预印本发布首个在2D PET上预训练的DINOv2模型，并与原版DINOv2、OmniRad在分类、分割与预后任务上对比。
key_points: 首个2D PET预训练的DINOv2模型
统一轻量头对比三个编码器

reason: 有新意的预印本方法且有基线对比，但尚未经同行评审、任务验证范围有限
abstract: DINO (self-DIstillation with NO labels) has become a stan- dard for self-supervised pre-training, producing features that generalise across datasets and downstream tasks. In medical imaging it has been adopted mainly for radiology (X-ray, CT and MRI), where even natural- image DINO features transfer well. In the literature, these features have been reported to transfer worse to functional imaging such as PET. Yet PET-specific DINO models have barely been introduced, and even less validated across multiple tasks and datasets. We present PET-DINOv2-2D, the first DINOv2 model pre-trained on 2D PET, and benchmark it against open-source encoders: the origi- nal DINOv2 (pre-trained on the LVD-142M natural-image dataset) and OmniRad (pre-trained on CT, MRI and ultrasound). Using the same lightweight heads for every backbone, and despite far less pre-training data, PET-DINOv2-2D matches or outperforms both on three down- stream PET tasks: normal/abnormal classification, lesion segmentation and recurrence-free survival prognosis. Its advantage is largest when few labels are available, suggesting that PET pre-training gives more transferable, label-efficient features. Code is made available at https://github.com/nuclivision/pet-dinov2-2d/.
zh_abstract: DINO（self-DIstillation with NO labels，无标签自蒸馏）已成为自监督预训练的标准，所产生的特征能够泛化到不同数据集和下游任务。在医学影像中，它主要用于放射学（X 射线、CT 和 MRI），即使自然图像 DINO 特征也能很好地迁移。文献报道，这些特征向 PET 等功能成像的迁移效果较差。然而，PET 专用的 DINO 模型几乎尚未被提出，更少在多个任务和数据集上得到验证。我们提出 PET-DINOv2-2D，这是首个在 2D PET 上预训练的 DINOv2 模型，并将其与开源编码器进行基准比较：原始 DINOv2（在 LVD-142M 自然图像数据集上预训练）和 OmniRad（在 CT、MRI 和超声上预训练）。对每个骨干网络使用相同的轻量级头，尽管预训练数据少得多，PET-DINOv2-2D 在三个下游 PET 任务上达到或超过二者：正常/异常分类、病灶分割和无复发生存预后。其优势在可用标签较少时最大，提示 PET 预训练能提供更具迁移性、标签效率更高的特征。代码已在 https://github.com/nuclivision/pet-dinov2-2d/ 提供。

source: PubMed · Journal of medical Internet research

abstract: [Journal of medical Internet research] AI-enabled patient profiling has been proposed to organize heterogeneous patient data and support personalized nursing care and health support. Given the growing use of AI, machine learning, large language models (LLMs), digital phenotyping, and digital twins in health care, it is important to clarify how patient profiling has been conceptualized, applied, and evaluated in nursing-relevant contexts. This scoping review aimed to examine and report the available evidence on AI-enabled patient profiling for personalized nursing care and health support. This scoping review was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodological framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews). Chinese and English databases were searched from inception to May 18, 2026, including China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, VIP Database, Chinese Biomedical Literature Database, PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Embase. Eligible studies used AI or computational intelligence methods to construct, classify, apply, validate, or evaluate patient profiles or related patient representations relevant to personalized nursing care or health support. Two reviewers independently screened records, assessed full texts, and charted data using a predefined form. Data were synthesized descriptively and narratively using an input-process-output framework. A total of 61 studies were included. AI-enabled patient profiling was represented through patient profiles, patient or user personas, digital phenotypes, patient segments, clinical subtypes, digital twins, and LLM-enabled personalization. Included studies used diverse data sources, including electronic health records, nursing records, patient-reported outcomes, questionnaires, mobile app data, wearable and sensor data, engagement logs, and textual or conversational data. Common AI approaches included machine learning, clustering, deep learning, natural language processing, recommender systems, knowledge graphs, digital twin modeling, and LLMs. Applications focused on personalized education, self-management support, rehabilitation, chronic disease management, remote monitoring, decision support, follow-up care, and shared decision-making. zh_abstract: [Journal of Medical Internet Research] 已提出AI赋能的患者画像，用于组织异质性患者数据并支持个性化护理和健康支持。鉴于AI、机器学习、大语言模型（LLMs）、数字表型分析和数字孪生在医疗保健中的使用日益增多，有必要明确患者画像在护理相关情境中是如何被概念化、应用和评价的。本范围综述旨在审查并报告关于AI赋能患者画像用于个性化护理和健康支持的可获得证据。本范围综述采用Joanna Briggs Institute方法学框架和PRISMA-ScR（Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews）进行。检索中文和英文数据库，时间自建库至2026年5月18日，包括中国知网（China National Knowledge Infrastructure）、万方数据（Wanfang Data）、维普数据库（VIP Database）、中国生物医学文献数据库（Chinese Biomedical Literature Database）、PubMed、CINAHL、Web of Science和Embase。符合条件的研究使用AI或计算智能方法构建、分类、应用、验证或评价与个性化护理或健康支持相关的患者画像或相关患者表征。两名评价者独立筛选记录、评估全文，并使用预定义表格提取数据。采用输入-过程-输出框架对数据进行描述性和叙述性综合。共纳入61项研究。AI赋能的患者画像通过患者画像、患者或用户角色画像、数字表型、患者分群、临床亚型、数字孪生和LLM赋能的个性化来体现。纳入研究使用了多种数据来源，包括电子健康记录、护理记录、患者报告结局、问卷、移动应用数据、可穿戴设备和传感器数据、参与日志以及文本或对话数据。常见的AI方法包括机器学习、聚类、深度学习、自然语言处理、推荐系统、知识图谱、数字孪生建模和LLMs。应用集中于个性化教育、自我管理支持、康复、慢性病管理、远程监测、决策支持、随访照护和共享决策。大多数研究评价了算法性能、可行性、可用性或系统开发，而较少研究考察了画像有效性、可操作性、公平性、工作流程整合或长期护理敏感

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: The First Hospital of Jilin University; conditions: Acute Thoraco-Abdominal Emergency Lesions; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 640; status: RECRUITING] This is a single-center, prospective, stratified 1:1 parallel-group randomized superiority diagnostic trial at The First Hospital of Jilin University. Eligible emergency patients aged ≥18 who received routine thoraco-abdominal non-contrast CT were randomly assigned to two groups. The experimental group adopted a self-developed vision-language large model (powER) for auxiliary CT interpretation, while the control group received standard radiological reading without AI assistance. All participants completed standardized 60-day clinical follow-up to obtain clinical gold-standard outcomes. The primary objective is to compare the diagnostic performance of the AI model versus conventional radiology interpretation for multiple acute thoraco-abdominal emergency lesions.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Thyroid Nodule Diagnosis: From Multimodal Integration to Clinical Utility.
zh_title: 甲状腺结节诊断AI：从多模态整合到临床效用
summary: 叙述性综述评估超声、细胞学、组织学与分子模型的AI研究，主张以决策改变而非单一准确率衡量价值。
abstract: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] Artificial intelligence (AI) for thyroid nodules should be evaluated against the decisions it changes, not diagnostic accuracy alone. This critical narrative review examines ultrasound, cytology, histology, and molecular models and distinguishes modality-specific prediction from implemented multimodal learning. The original PubMed/MEDLINE search through 10 August 2026 was supplemented on 25 September 2026 by targeted OpenAlex searches and checks of primary publications, reporting standards, and regulatory sources. Selected studies are compared by sample size, reference standard, acquisition setting, testing design, and performance with confidence intervals where available. We explain feature concatenation, intermediate representation learning, cross-attention, and decision-level fusion, and examine whether integration improves on the strongest component. Reported gains are inconsistent, and complete-case multimodal datasets may exclude the low-risk nodules most relevant to avoiding biopsy. High discrimination for histological malignancy or occult nodal disease does not demonstrate reduced overdiagnosis, fewer operations, or improved survival. A thyroid-specific translation roadmap therefore addresses active surveillance, partial verification and spectrum bias, Hashimoto thyroiditis and multinodular disease, cytology preparation shifts, category-specific thresholds, operator dependence, reporting frameworks, and regulatory change control. The priority is a calibrated, externally tested tool using information available at a defined clinical decision, followed by prospective evaluation of patient and workflow outcomes. A unified imaging-pathology-omics system and reliable AI prediction of surveillance progression remain research objectives rather than established clinical capabilities.

zh_abstract: [Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland)] 对甲状腺结节的人工智能（AI）应依据其改变的决策来评估，而不仅仅是诊断准确率。这篇批判性叙述性综述考察超声、细胞学、组织学和分子模型，并区分特定模态预测与已实施的多模态学习。原始 PubMed/MEDLINE 检索截至 2026 年 8 月 10 日，并于 2026 年 9 月 25 日通过有针对性的 OpenAlex 检索以及对原始出版物、报告标准和监管来源的核查进行补充。所选研究按样本量、参考标准、采集环境、测试设计以及（若有）带置信区间的性能进行比较。我们解释特征拼接、中间表示学习、交叉注意力和决策级融合，并考察整合是否优于最强组件。报道的增益并不一致，完整病例多模态数据集可能排除与避免活检最相关的低风险结节。对组织学恶性或隐匿性淋巴结病变的高区分度并不能证明可减少过度诊断、减少手术或改善生存。因此，针对甲状腺的转化路线图涉及主动监测、部分验证和谱偏倚、桥本甲状腺炎和多结节性疾病、细胞学制片变化、类别特异性阈值、操作者依赖性、报告框架和监管变更控制。优先事项是使用在明确临床决策时可获得的信息，开发经过校准和外部测试的工具，随后对患者和工作流程结局进行前瞻性评估。统一的影像-病理-组学系统以及对监测进展的可靠 AI 预测仍是研究目标，而非已确立的临床能力。

title: Integrating Heterogeneous Echocardiography AI Outputs in Language Space: Learnable Late Fusion with a Supervised LLM
zh_title: 用监督式LLM在语言空间融合超声心动图AI输出
summary: 预印本提出基于监督式大语言模型的后期融合模块，在语言空间聚合视图特异的超声心动图AI结论与测量值。
key_points: 直接融合各视图预测描述与测量值而非二值决策
859次检查、646例患者的三折交叉验证
性能与最佳参考策略相当，优于无监督通用LLM
reason: 预印本新方法有基线对比，但仅内部交叉验证、无外部验证，属值得一看档
abstract: View- and target-specific echocardiography AI models capture useful but complementary information and may not achieve sufficient predictive performance in isolation. A learned ensemble is a natural way to combine these outputs, but heterogeneous models typically require each output to be converted into a binary decision, probability, confidence score, or fixed-length feature vector. We developed a supervised large language model (LLM)-based late-fusion module that directly aggregates view-specific predicted finding statements and predicted measurements in language space and learns a case-level fusion function. In patient-level three-fold cross-validation of 859 examinations from 646 patients, the proposed method integrated heterogeneous outputs within a single framework, performed comparably to the best-performing reference strategy evaluated, and outperformed a general-purpose LLM without task-specific training. These results suggest that a supervised LLM can combine multiple upstream models without model-specific output conversion or feature engineering that requires medical knowledge.
zh_abstract: 视图特异性和目标特异性的超声心动图AI模型可捕捉有用但互补的信息，并且单独使用时可能无法达到足够的预测性能。学习型集成是组合这些输出的一种自然方式，但异构模型通常要求将每个输出转换为二元决策、概率、置信度分数或固定长度特征向量。我们开发了一个基于监督式大语言模型（large language model, LLM）的后期融合模块，该模块在语言空间中直接聚合视图特异性的预测发现陈述和预测测量值，并学习病例级融合函数。在来自646例患者的859次检查的患者水平三折交叉验证中，所提出的方法在单一框架内整合了异构输出，其表现与所评估的表现最佳的参考策略相当，并优于未经任务特定训练的通用LLM。这些结果提示，监督式LLM可以组合多个上游模型，而无需进行模型特定的输出转换或需要医学知识的特征工程。

key_points: 覆盖AD、PPA、bvFTD、DLB与帕金森病

abstract: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Istituti Clinici Scientifici Maugeri SpA; conditions: Alzheimer's Disease (AD), Frontotemporal Dementia (FTD), Parkinsons Disease (PD), Lewy Body Dementia; type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 200; status: RECRUITING] This multicenter study aims to characterize the language profiles of patients with various neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), Primary Progressive Aphasia (PPA), behavioral variant Frontotemporal Dementia (bvFTD), Dementia with Lewy Bodies (DLB), and Parkinson's disease (PD), using artificial intelligence (AI) models. By analyzing speech and language data collected during remote neuropsychological assessments, the researchers intend to identify objective linguistic biomarkers suitable for early and differential diagnosis, overcoming the limitations of traditional, invasive, and costly diagnostic tools. The project will develop and validate an AI-driven pipeline to provide scalable and individualized linguistic profiles, ultimately supporting personalized treatment strategies and improving clinical workflow efficiency in the Italian population.
zh_abstract: [新注册临床试验，尚无结果；申办者：Istituti Clinici Scientifici Maugeri SpA；疾病：阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's Disease, AD）、额颞叶痴呆（Frontotemporal Dementia, FTD）、帕金森病（Parkinsons Disease, PD）、路易体痴呆（Lewy Body Dementia）；类型：干预性；分期：NA；入组人数：200；状态：招募中] 这项多中心研究旨在使用人工智能（artificial intelligence, AI）模型，刻画多种神经退行性疾病患者的语言特征，包括阿尔茨海默病（Alzheimer's disease, AD）、原发性进行性失语（Primary Progressive Aphasia, PPA）、行为变异型额颞叶痴呆（behavioral variant Frontotemporal Dementia, bvFTD）、路易体痴呆（Dementia with Lewy Bodies, DLB）和帕金森病（Parkinson's disease, PD）。通过分析在远程神经心理评估期间收集的言语和语言数据，研究人员打算识别适用于早期诊断和鉴别诊断的客观语言生物标志物，克服传统诊断工具有创且昂贵的局限性。该项目将开发并验证一个由AI驱动的流程，以提供可扩展且个体化的语言画像，最终支持个性化治疗策略并提高意大利人群的临床工作流程效率。
